name: LumenCache
author: Celsius Anderson

sections.description:
LumenCache implements a RAM-first full-page cache with a WordPress
advanced-cache.php drop-in. On a cache HIT, the drop-in serves complete HTML
before the normal WordPress bootstrap and database queries. This early-response
path reduces application-layer work and keeps repeat page requests fast across
Nginx, Apache, and LiteSpeed.

The cache is designed to fail open when its storage layer is unavailable, so a
cache connection problem does not take the WordPress site offline.

Research Foundation

Academic Reference:
“Dynamic Resource Mapping in Zero-Reload Server Architectures: Eliminating
Application-Layer Latency and Extension Dependency in High-Concurrency CMS
personalised requests continue through the full WordPress stack.

This architecture is intended to reduce repeated bootstrap work, database
queries, and extension overhead while preserving WordPress compatibility. It
also provides a practical bridge between academic performance research and
everyday publishing workloads, including content-heavy sites, WooCommerce
catalogues, and membership-driven pages.

Research author: Dean Nasrul Eam — Light & Composition University.

Eight-Subsystem Architecture

  1. RAM-First Full-Page Cache Engine — PHP stores complete HTML at
    shutdown and resolves repeat requests from the in-memory cache layer.
  2. Nginx / Apache Proxy Bridge — Static or dynamic server config bypasses
    PHP entirely for cache hits.
  3. Selective Bypass Cookie Router — sys_active_state cookie routes
    logged-in users and cart-active visitors to live PHP.
  4. Application Driver Profile Engine — Auto-detects WooCommerce,
    LearnDash, LifterLMS, MemberPress, BuddyBoss and registers tailored bypass
    rules and invalidation hooks.
  5. Surgical Cache Invalidation — Post save / nav menu / widget / theme
    switch events trigger precise per-URL or full purges.
  6. REST API State Endpoint — /wp-json/lumencache/v1/user-state serves
    personalised fragments for skeleton-hydration clients.
  7. Skeleton Hydration DOM Worker — skeleton-hydration.js replaces cached
    placeholders with live content on load.
  8. WP-CLI Management Interface — flush, flush-url, status commands.

Configuration (optional)

All settings are configurable from LumenCache → Settings in the WordPress
admin. Optionally override any setting via wp-config.php — constants always win:

define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_HOST',          '127.0.0.1' );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_PORT',          6379 );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_SOCKET',        '' );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_PASSWORD',      '' );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_DATABASE',      0 );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT',       1.0 );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_PREFIX',        'cache:' );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_CACHE_TTL',           86400 );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_CACHE_SALT',          '' );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_CACHE_QUERY_STRINGS', false );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_PROXY_PASSWORD',      '' );

WP-CLI

wp lumencache flush
wp lumencache flush-url https://example.com/page/
wp lumencache status<h3>Privacy</h3>

LumenCache stores rendered page HTML and cache metadata in the in-memory cache
service configured by the site administrator. It does not send cache contents,
visitor data, or analytics data to a third-party LumenCache service. The
optional user-state endpoint returns only the requested dynamic values to the
requesting browser; sites should review those values and their own privacy
policy before enabling personalized hydration.

Current Active Pipeline Status — LumenCache + LumenCache Pro (August 8, 2026)

Audited release: LumenCache 1.6.3 / LumenCache Pro 1.0.5. Every listed
pipeline was read from its UI/request entry point through configuration,
runtime, failures, persistence, invalidation, and visible output.

  • Pre-WordPress readers (drop-in and Apache proxy): fixed Redis timeout,
    Predis availability, boolean configuration parsing, empty-value reader
    parity, and safety bypasses for dynamic/personal routes. Confirmed tracking
    key stripping and Redis key construction agree with the write path.
  • Capture and Redis write: fixed non-HTML response rejection; full-page
    cache stores only HTML that early readers can safely replay.
  • Local invalidation and purge controls: fixed relative URL, host/scheme,
    trailing-slash, and tracking-query normalization so admin/CLI/post purges
    target the same key cache writes create.
  • Server integration and lifecycle: fixed foreign drop-in overwrite; LumenCache
    owns/removes only its own file. Generated Apache/Nginx configuration and
    existing salt safety behavior were read directly.
  • Application drivers and state routing: fixed early-reader parity for
    WooCommerce, LMS, membership, Buddy/BuddyPress, and LCU routes/cookies; no
    longer clears active-session state on completion events that do not end access.
  • Administration, REST, CLI, updates: verified capability/nonce boundaries;
    fixed REST personalized-state access, update-domain identity/PHP metadata,
    LumenCache screen asset scoping, and visible drop-in conflict feedback.
  • Pro entitlement, telemetry, Cloudflare, updates and UI: fixed
    constant-license update eligibility and Cloudflare token page-source exposure.
    Local-first then best-effort edge invalidation and license status/drop-in
    synchronization were verified.
  • Intentional constraints retained: domain-only license authorization and
    the optional direct-Redis Nginx tracking-parameter limitation remain
    unchanged by design. Standard Nginx cannot use salted SHA-256 keys without
    the documented OpenResty/Lua route.
  • Validation: focused regression contracts pass (13 tests / 60 assertions);
    all LumenCache and LumenCache Pro PHP files lint clean. A real
    WordPress+Redis+Cloudflare server remains required to prove live edge/API
    behavior after installation.
sections.faq:
Why are 0 pages cached?

Two common causes:
1. Nginx config not applied — visit Server Setup and paste the config blocks.
2. WooCommerce session cookie — fixed in v1.1.0. Previous versions bypassed
the cache for all visitors on WooCommerce sites due to the always-present
wp_woocommerce_session_* cookie.

Why can key salting affect server-level caching?

When LUMENCACHE_CACHE_SALT is set, PHP stores keys as SHA-256 hashes. A
server-level configuration must use the same key strategy or it will produce
cache misses. Disable the salt for a plain-key configuration, or use the
compatible hashed-key server template.

Does LumenCache work with LiteSpeed?

Yes. LiteSpeed supports Apache-compatible .htaccess rewrites. LumenCache uses
the Apache proxy mode on LiteSpeed. For better performance, ask your host
which in-memory cache acceleration options are available.

Can I still use wp-config.php constants?

Yes — constants always take precedence over admin settings. If you define a
constant, the corresponding field in the Settings tab is shown locked (read-only).
sections.changelog:
1.6.23 (August 15, 2026) – Security Hardening & Direct Access Prevention

  • SECURITY — Added explicit ABSPATH direct file access prevention guard to server/lumen-cache-proxy.php to prevent direct unauthenticated HTTP script execution.
  • APACHE DEPLOYER — Updated Htaccess::deploy_proxy() to automatically configure localized ABSPATH definitions upon file deployment.

1.6.22 (August 15, 2026) – WordPress.org Guideline 5 Compliance & Clean UI

  • COMPLIANCE — Full compliance with WordPress.org Guideline 5 (Trialware & Locked Features): removed all locked feature tabs and upsell screens from the free Standard edition.
  • UX — Added clean external outbound link button “Upgrade to Pro ↗” linking directly to the product page (https://www.lightandcomposition.com/dev/lumencache/).
  • UX — Added passive informational card at the bottom of the Overview tab.
  • CONTRIBUTORS — Updated Contributors list in readme.txt to nasruleam, celsiusanderson.
  • DROP-IN — Dropped external config file requirement; advanced-cache.php is now completely self-contained with compiled configuration snapshot data.
  • SANITIZATION — Added strict input and header sanitization against CRLF injection across all pre-bootstrap request paths.

1.6.21 (August 14, 2026) – Plugin URI Fix

  • HOUSEKEEPING — Plugin URI now points to the plugin’s own Dev Lab page (/dev/lumencache/) instead of a GitHub repo link, matching Standard/Pro edition parity across the catalog.

1.6.20 (August 11, 2026) – Quick Setup Tracker UI Fix

  • FIX — Synced Quick Setup step flex rules (flex: 0 0 auto for non-active steps and flex: 1 1 220px for active step) in assets/css/admin.css with Smart Media Redirect Cleaner to prevent connector lines (.lc-qs-line) from overlapping step text.

1.6.19 (August 11, 2026) – Pipeline 5: Apache Proxy Critical Fixes

  • FIX CRITICAL — lumen-cache-proxy.php used sanitize_text_field() / wp_unslash() — WP functions unavailable when proxy runs (invoked directly by Apache mod_rewrite before WP loads). Replaced with native PHP casts.
  • FIX CRITICAL — All require __DIR__ . '/index.php' in proxy pointed to uploads directory. WordPress index.php is at ABSPATH (two levels up). Fixed using LUMENCACHE_PROXY_ABSPATH.
  • FIX CRITICAL — wp-config.php path pointed to uploads dir. Fixed to LUMENCACHE_PROXY_ABSPATH . 'wp-config.php'.
  • FIX CRITICAL — lumen-cache-config.php path resolved to uploads/wp-content/... (non-existent). Fixed to dirname(__DIR__) . '/lumen-cache-config.php'.

1.6.18 (August 11, 2026) – Pipeline 4: Redis Connector Fixes

  • FIX — connect_phpredis() now checks return value of $redis->auth() and throws on false (wrong password). Previously, a bad password silently left the connection open but all commands would fail with NOAUTH errors, making caching silently non-functional.
  • FIX — connect_phpredis() now checks return value of $redis->select() and throws on false (invalid database index).

1.6.17 (August 11, 2026) – Pipeline 3: Cache Engine Audit

  • PERF FIX — Debug string concatenation in start_capture() and maybe_write_cache() was evaluated on every page load even with LUMENCACHE_DEBUG=false. Now guarded behind an explicit debug check. Zero overhead on production sites.
  • AUDIT — Full cache engine logic (bypass rules, key building, invalidation, tracking-param stripping, output buffer capture) verified. No logic bugs found.

1.6.16 (August 11, 2026) – Pipeline 2: Drop-in & Config Critical Fixes

  • FIX CRITICAL — advanced-cache.php called sanitize_text_field() and wp_unslash() before WordPress loads. These functions don’t exist at drop-in execution time, causing Fatal Errors on every page load. Replaced with native PHP (string) casts and isset() guards.
  • FIX CRITICAL — Drop_In::enable_wp_cache() used str_replace($marker,$snippet,$content,$count) — PHP does not support a 4th count argument in str_replace(). $count was always 0, so WP_CACHE was never written to wp-config.php. Fixed using substr_count() + substr_replace().
  • MINOR — advanced-cache.php internal version bumped to v1.2.6.

1.6.15 (August 11, 2026) – Pipeline 1: Bootstrap & Lifecycle Fixes

  • FIX — Lifecycle::uninstall() now flushes all LumenCache Redis keys before removing plugin files, preventing stale cached HTML from persisting after reinstalls.
  • FIX — Lifecycle::uninstall() now deletes the lumencache_pro_status WP option to fully clean up Pro licensing state on uninstall.
  • FIX — Corrected stale comment in Lifecycle::deactivate() that incorrectly referred to “ABSPATH” for proxy file location.
  • FIX — Settings::effective_connection() now correctly returns 'manual' as source for hand-entered TCP host/port settings instead of misleading 'auto'.

1.6.12 (August 10, 2026) – WooCommerce cart-fragments guard

  • NEW — built-in guard against crawler-triggered WooCommerce cart-fragment
    storms. Cached pages are served to cookieless visitors (bots, first-time
    viewers) with the wc-cart-fragments script embedded; every crawler that
    executes it fires an uncacheable POST /?wc-ajax=get_refreshed_fragments
    that boots full WordPress + WooCommerce just to render an empty mini-cart.
    One crawler generated 59,000 such requests in seven hours on a single site.
    LumenCache now (1) omits the fragments script for visitors with no
    WooCommerce session/cart cookie and no login, and (2) answers cookieless
    fragment requests with a static empty-fragments JSON before WooCommerce
    builds the cart. Cart and checkout pages always keep the script, and real
    shoppers (any WooCommerce cookie) are never affected. Disable via:
    add_filter( ‘lumencache_woo_fragments_guard’, ‘__return_false’ );

1.6.11 (August 9, 2026) – WordPress.org compliance + attribution

  • REMOVED — the private update checker (class-lc-updates.php). WordPress.org
    does not permit custom plugin updaters in directory-hosted plugins; the
    Standard build now relies solely on the WordPress.org update channel.
    License-gated private updates remain available for LumenCache Pro only.
  • IMPROVED — the Hosting Guide’s Plesk section now gives direct SSH install
    instructions (apt install redis-server / yum install redis) since there is
    no direct Redis extension for Plesk.
  • IMPROVED — the dashboard header now credits the plugin author, the
    Light & Composition University Dev Lab, and links the peer-reviewed
    research journal article the architecture is based on.

1.6.10 (August 9, 2026) – RAM Cache Engine step + Hosting Guide

  • NEW — Quick Setup now has a fifth step “RAM Cache Engine” as the first item.
    It checks whether the in-memory backend is reachable. If not connected, the
    green “fully configured” success row is suppressed — the tracker shows the
    backend step as the active item to resolve, with shortcuts to the Connection
    tab and the new Hosting Guide. A site with an unreachable backend can never
    claim to be fully configured.
  • NEW — “Hosting Guide” tab added to the left panel sidebar. Covers how to
    check and request Redis on cPanel/shared hosting (with a copy-ready provider
    email template), managed WordPress hosts (Kinsta, WP Engine, Cloudways,
    Pressable), VPS/Plesk with root access (install commands), and what to
    expect if the host cannot provide Redis at all.

1.6.9 (August 9, 2026) – Quick Setup review for active sites

  • IMPROVED — fully configured sites now keep the green success row but also
    offer a “View all setup steps” control. Expanding it shows all four
    completed Quick Setup steps, and every circle and label remains linked to
    its existing Settings or Server Setup section. The tracker stays compact
    by default and is responsive on narrow screens.

1.6.8 (August 9, 2026) – Quick Setup progress tracker

  • NEW — a four-step Quick Setup tracker now appears on the Overview tab,
    directly below the metrics band, until setup is complete: 1) Enable RAM
    Cache (deploy the drop-in), 2) Activate Boot Hook (WP_CACHE), 3) Security
    Hardening (key salt), 4) Server Ready (.htaccess rules on Apache/LiteSpeed;
    on Nginx either the direct bridge without a salt — which marks Security
    Hardening as not applicable, since standard Nginx cannot compute salted
    keys — or the salted PHP drop-in path. Salt + active bridge is flagged as
    a conflict, never counted as complete, and bridge removal is re-verified
    live so a stale status cannot keep the warning around).
    Completed steps show a green checkmark; the
    current step is highlighted and explains what it does. Steps 1 and 2 offer
    a one-click Enable button right in the tracker; every step is clickable
    and jumps to the relevant sidebar section. Once all four steps are done
    the tracker collapses to a single “fully configured” success row, which
    can be expanded to review and navigate through all four completed steps.

1.6.7 (August 9, 2026) – aligned Pro card headers

  • FIX — Pro badges, card titles, and Active/Inactive status pills now sit on
    one aligned row across the Pro License, Cache Telemetry, Effective Settings,
    Config Checker, and Advanced Settings screens. Descriptive metadata remains
    below the header row and wraps cleanly on narrow screens.

1.6.6 (August 8, 2026) – pipeline-by-pipeline audit: Server Setup

  • SECURITY/PRIVACY FIX — the generated Nginx direct-Redis map block and the
    generated .htaccess Apache/LiteSpeed bypass rules only matched
    MemberPress session cookies starting with mepr_. The PHP-side
    MemberPress driver (class-app-drivers.php) has always also matched
    memberpress_-prefixed cookies. On any site whose MemberPress cookie used
    that alternate prefix, Nginx direct-Redis mode or the Apache/LiteSpeed
    rewrite proxy would have served a cached, non-personalized page straight
    to a logged-in member instead of bypassing to PHP. Both generators now
    emit the missing condition, matching the PHP driver exactly.
  • FIX — the same gap (plus a stale wp_woocommerce_session_ bypass that
    would have defeated caching for 100% of anonymous WooCommerce visitors)
    existed in the static reference config files
    (server-configs/nginx/nginx-global-template.conf and
    nginx-per-site-example.conf) shown to admins during manual Nginx setup;
    corrected to match the live generated map exactly.
  • CLEANUP — removed server-configs/apache/apache-redis-proxy.php and
    apache-redis-cache.conf: a stale, unreferenced duplicate of the real
    deployed proxy (server/lumen-cache-proxy.php, wired through
    Htaccess::PROXY_FILENAME) that was missing the tracking-parameter
    stripping and MemberPress-cookie fixes already present in the real file —
    keeping it around risked a future maintainer editing the wrong copy.
  • AUDIT — read the full Server Setup pipeline end-to-end: drop-in/WP_CACHE/
    config-file status detection, the Nginx map + server block generators, the
    Apache/LiteSpeed .htaccess rewrite rules, the real deployed Redis proxy,
    and panel-specific setup instructions (Plesk/cPanel/DirectAdmin/manual).
    Confirmed the Nginx server-block’s manually-built $redis_key (prefix +
    scheme+method+host+uri) exactly matches what Redis_Connector produces in
    PHP (prefix applied by the connector wrapper + build_nginx_key()‘s raw
    components) — no other mismatches found.

1.6.5 (August 8, 2026) – pipeline-by-pipeline audit: stale Pro-nav references

  • FIX — after the Pro sidebar was split into five separate nav pages
    (License / Telemetry / Effective Settings / Config Checker / Advanced
    Settings), the Settings tab’s license status card still told active-Pro
    admins to “manage your license from the Pro Controls section below” — a
    section that no longer exists. Now points to the correct “Pro License”
    sidebar page.
  • FIX — three internal doc comments (in the main plugin file and the admin
    class) still referenced the removed lc_render_pro_panel() function and
    lumencache_render_pro_panel action by name; updated to the five current
    per-feature function/action names so future maintenance isn’t misled.
  • AUDIT — read every function behind the Connection, Cache Controls,
    Settings, and Overview nav pages end-to-end: verified the manual “Purge
    URL” form builds the exact same Redis key (scheme + host + path,
    trailing-slash and tracking-param normalized) as the page-write path, so a
    manual purge always hits the real cached entry; no other bugs found in
    these four pipelines.

1.6.4 (August 8, 2026) – UX: one nav item per Pro feature

  • Split the combined “Pro Controls” admin page into five separate sidebar
    pages (Pro License, Cache Telemetry, Effective Settings, Config Checker,
    Advanced Settings), matching LC SEO Optimizer’s one-feature-one-nav-link
    pattern. See LumenCache Pro changelog for the corresponding hook changes.

1.6.3 (August 8, 2026) – sequential end-to-end cache safety audit

  • CRITICAL FIX — the PHP drop-in no longer overwrites another cache plugin’s
    wp-content/advanced-cache.php. Deployment now stops with a clear conflict
    instead of destroying another plugin’s pre-WordPress cache layer.
  • FIX — aligned the WordPress drop-in, Apache proxy, and canonical connector:
    generated configuration now carries the Redis timeout; all readers use the
    same 1-second default; the drop-in can use an already-available Predis client;
    and the proxy correctly reads literal true / false wp-config constants.
  • SECURITY FIX — early readers now bypass cart, checkout, account, LMS,
    membership, Buddy/BuddyPress, and LCU course routes before WordPress boots,
    and the Apache proxy now mirrors logged-in/cart/LMS/member cookie bypasses.
    The active-session cookie is no longer cleared merely because a purchase or
    course/lesson completes.
  • FIX — cache writes reject successful non-HTML responses, preventing a later
    early cache hit from replaying JSON, XML, feeds, or downloads as text/html.
  • FIX — URL purges now use the same site-host, trailing-slash, and
    tracking-parameter normalization as cache writes. Relative admin/CLI URLs
    and URLs carrying gclid, fbclid, or other stripped tracking tokens now
    remove the real cache key.
  • SECURITY FIX — guest skeleton hydration is limited to cart values from the
    caller’s own WooCommerce session; member, course-progress, and notification
    values require an authenticated WordPress REST nonce. Update checks use the
    configured site domain and update information correctly declares PHP 8.1.
  • UI FIX — admin scripts/styles load only on LumenCache’s own screen, and
    drop-in deployment failures now return a visible reason.

1.6.2

  • ADDED: a private update delivery channel via LC License Manager.
    (Removed again in 1.6.11 for WordPress.org directory compliance.)

1.6.1

  • Replaced anchor-link scroll navigation with instant click-to-show tabs across the dashboard (Overview, Connection, Cache Controls, Settings, Server Setup, and Pro Controls), matching the LC SEO Optimizer UX.
  • Fixed the WP admin bar “Server Setup” quick link, which pointed at a stale tab slug and no longer opened the right tab.

1.6.0

  • Major architecture change: LumenCache is now split into two plugins, mirroring the
    Spam Account Defender Standard/Pro pattern. This plugin (Standard) no longer has any
    hard PHP class dependency on Pro code — Pro features are provided entirely by the new
    companion plugin, “LumenCache Pro” (lumen-cache-pro/), which hooks into a documented
    set of actions/filters (lumencache_render_pro_panel, lumencache_has_pro_feature,
    lumencache_record_bypass/_miss/_write_failure, lumencache_purge_urls,
    lumencache_after_flush_all, lumencache_dashboard_widget_pro_rows,
    lumencache_cloudflare_is_configured, lumencache_base_plugin_ready).
  • Admin dashboard rebuilt as a sidebar-navigation single-page shell (Overview, Connection,
    Cache Controls, Settings, Server Setup, Pro) replacing the old top-tab layout, matching
    the Spam Account Defender dashboard’s visual style, including a collapsible sidebar.
  • License activation, telemetry, Cloudflare integration, config-consistency checker, and
    advanced Redis/Cloudflare settings now live entirely in LumenCache Pro; install and
    activate LumenCache Pro to keep using these features (no data migration needed — Pro
    reads/writes the same settings and Redis telemetry keys as before).
  • No changes to core caching behavior, Redis connection logic, or free-tier feature set.

1.5.1

  • FIX: Htaccess::server_label() checked for “litespeed” before “openlitespeed”,
    so every OpenLiteSpeed install was mislabeled as commercial LiteSpeed in the
    Dashboard tab (the substring “litespeed” is contained inside “openlitespeed”).
    The more specific check now runs first.
  • FIX: The generated Nginx per-site server block still emitted redis_pass
    and add_header X-Cache-Key $redis_key even when a Cache Salt was
    configured, referencing an $redis_key variable that was never defined in
    that case (the salted branch only emitted comments). Pasting that block
    into Nginx would fail to load. The salted case now emits a safe,
    fully-commented placeholder pointing at the OpenResty/Lua variant instead.
  • FIX: The generated Nginx map block and .htaccess rewrite rules bypassed
    the cache on the mere presence of woocommerce_items_in_cart /
    woocommerce_cart_hash cookies, unlike the PHP-side bypass rule in
    class-app-drivers.php (v1.1.0) which requires a non-zero/non-empty value.
    Both server-level rules now require the same non-zero/non-empty value.
  • Housekeeping: full pipeline audit of the Cloudflare purge feature, the
    license/Pro layer, and every core-engine include added in 1.4.0–1.5.0; no
    further bugs found outside the three above.

1.5.0

  • NEW (Pro): Cloudflare edge cache purging. Enter a Cloudflare API Token
    (Zone → Cache Purge permission) and Zone ID in Settings → Cloudflare
    Integration. When enabled, “Flush All Cache” purges the local Redis cache
    and Cloudflare’s edge cache together, and a separate “Purge Cloudflare
    Cache” button on the Dashboard tab purges Cloudflare on its own. Includes a
    Test Connection button to verify credentials before relying on them.
    New class Cloudflare_Connector (includes/class-cloudflare-connector.php).
    Best-effort: a Cloudflare purge failure never blocks or hides a successful
    local flush.

1.4.0

  • NEW: LumenCache Pro — per-customer license engine, Pro capability layer,
    telemetry/diagnostics, and Redis connection test UI. Free/core behavior is
    completely unchanged when Pro is not active.
  • NEW: lc-license-manager v1.4.0 — real per-customer license engine
    (LC_License_Engine): unique LC-XXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX keys, per-license
    domain-activation limits, idempotent issuance per order, admin
    Licenses tab with search/pagination, manual test-license generator.
    Migration adds plugin_id, order_id, max_activations columns to
    wp_lc_licenses (guarded with SHOW COLUMNS pattern, safe to run on
    existing installs).
  • NEW: Pro class (includes/class-pro.php) — is_active() (hardcoded
    main-domain bypass, then LUMENCACHE_PRO_LICENSE constant, then DB-stored
    key), activate() / deactivate() with REST validation against
    lc-license/v1/validate, 6-hour transient cache, fail-open only on
    network/transport error (never on explicit invalid/revoked response).
  • NEW (Pro): Cache telemetry dashboard (P0.1) — hits, misses, hit ratio,
    bypass count, write-failures. HIT counting in advanced-cache.php via
    raw hIncrBy (pre-WP, reads pro_active from config snapshot); MISS/
    bypass/write-failure counted in Cache_Engine via Telemetry class.
    Redis hashes namespaced by site key prefix. Reset action included.
  • NEW (Pro): Bypass-reason diagnostics (P0.2) — per-reason counters in
    telemetry:bypass_reasons Redis hash; breakdown table in Pro dashboard.
  • NEW (Pro): Bot/origin-load guidance box (P0.3) — contextual panel
    computed from live counters; explains LumenCache scope vs Cloudflare/WAF.
  • NEW (Pro): WP_CACHE=false admin warning (P0.4) — shown above telemetry
    card when WP_CACHE is defined but false; links to existing Fix action.
  • NEW (Pro): Redis connection test button (P1.1) — “Test Connection” button
    on the Unix Socket field in Pro Settings; tests live without saving.
  • NEW (Pro): Effective-settings diagnostics table (P1.2) — shows effective
    value and override source (constant / database / default) for each setting.
  • NEW (Pro): Configuration consistency checker (P1.3) — flags
    WP_CACHE-off-but-dropin-deployed, salt+Nginx-direct conflict,
    socket+host both set, Redis database out of 0–15 range.
  • NEW: Subscription→license bridge in educational-products-for-woocommerce
    — PayPal subscription payment issues a license key and emails it;
    cancellation/expiration revokes it via LC_License_Engine.

1.3.0

  • NEW: Application Driver Profile Engine now auto-detects lc-seo-optimizer:
    • Registers a bypass pattern for its XML sitemap endpoints
      (/lcseo-sitemap.xml, /lcseo-sitemap-{type}.xml, and paginated
      variants) so plain-text XML is never served from an HTML cache entry —
      also hardcoded directly into advanced-cache.php and the Apache Redis
      proxy, since both drop-ins run before WordPress loads and cannot consult
      dynamically-registered bypass patterns.
    • Listens for two new custom actions lc-seo-optimizer now fires after its
      AJAX writes (lc_seo_metadata_updated, lc_seo_redirect_changed) and
      purges the affected page, or the whole cache when a pattern/bulk-import
      redirect change can’t be mapped to one URL.
  • IMPROVED: Redesigned the “Active Drivers” dashboard stat. It previously
    crammed every detected plugin into one ·-joined string inside a stats
    grid cell, which became unreadable past two or three drivers. It’s now a
    dedicated card below the stats grid, with each driver rendered as its own
    pill.

1.2.9

  • NEW: Application Driver Profile Engine now auto-detects the Light &
    Composition in-house plugin stack, the same way it already detects
    WooCommerce, LearnDash, LifterLMS, MemberPress, and BuddyBoss — no
    settings screen or manual configuration required:

    • Educational Products for WooCommerce (the in-house LCU LMS) —
      bypasses the /lccourse/ course/lesson routes and /my-courses/
      (personalised per-student progress and Global Access Hub grants), and
      registers purge rules for the edu_thesis and edu_journal CPTs, which
      are plain custom post types rather than WooCommerce products.
    • LC Award Management — registers purge rules for the lc_gear CPT
      and triggers a full purge on lc_award_metric_updated (social-share
      tracking, admin re-scoring, historical reseed), since leaderboard and
      Photo-of-the-Month pages are built from aggregate queries rather than a
      single permalink.
    • Photography Expeditions for WooCommerce — registers purge rules for
      the pew_booking CPT, which tracks availability/dates separately from
      the expedition WooCommerce product.
    • Art Photography for WooCommerce — detected for accurate dashboard
      and wp lumencache status reporting; limited-edition print data lives
      on the standard WooCommerce product CPT, which the WooCommerce driver
      already purges correctly.
      Detected in-house plugins now appear in the Dashboard, admin bar, and
      wp lumencache status output alongside the third-party integrations.

1.2.8

  • COMPATIBILITY: Tested up to WordPress 7.0.3. LumenCache’s custom admin
    pages (vanilla PHP templates, no WP_List_Table) render cleanly alongside
    the new DataViews React admin UI introduced in WordPress 7.0. No conflicts
    with the refreshed admin palette or JS module changes.
  • COMPATIBILITY: REST endpoint /wp-json/lumencache/v1/user-state confirmed
    compatible with WordPress 7.0 REST API and Interactivity API v2. Pages
    built with the Interactivity API serve identical HTML to anonymous visitors
    (personalized interactivity requires login, which already bypasses the
    cache), so full-page caching of Interactivity API pages is safe.
  • COMPATIBILITY: Tested on PHP 8.5.8 / PHP-FPM / Nginx FastCGI. All core
    paths (drop-in boot, Redis connector, cache engine, admin, WP-CLI) pass
    PHP 8.5 strict type and deprecation checks with no issues. Minimum
    requirement remains PHP 8.1.

1.2.7

  • FIX: enable_wp_cache() now handles all three states of WP_CACHE in
    wp-config.php instead of refusing to act when any existing definition is
    found:

    1. Not present at all → insert after <?php (original behaviour).
    2. Already true → nothing to do, return success immediately.
    3. Exists but false → overwrite with true using preg_replace.
      Case 3 fixes the WP Rocket conflict: WP Rocket writes
      define( ‘WP_CACHE’, false ); // Added by WP Rocket when its own page
      cache is disabled. The previous code detected “WP_CACHE” in the file and
      returned an error without fixing it, leaving the LumenCache drop-in unable
      to load on every subsequent request. LumenCache now takes ownership and
      corrects the value — the same approach WP Rocket, WP Super Cache, and
      WordPress core setup use.
  • NEW: disable_wp_cache() method removes the LumenCache-owned WP_CACHE line
    from wp-config.php on plugin deactivation and uninstall. Only lines
    carrying the “Added by LumenCache” comment are removed — defines placed by
    the user or another plugin are never touched.
  • Lifecycle::deactivate() and uninstall() now call Drop_In::disable_wp_cache()
    so wp-config.php is left clean after the plugin is removed.
  • DOCS: DOCUMENTATION.md updated to explain the wp-config.php write
    mechanism and the WP Rocket coexistence behaviour.

1.2.6

  • UX FIX: The Nginx salt-incompatibility warning was firing in PHP drop-in mode
    (any Nginx server) even though salt is completely compatible there — both the
    write path (class-cache-engine.php) and the read path (advanced-cache.php)
    compute the same SHA-256 hash, so keys always match. Salt is only broken when
    Nginx direct-Redis mode is active (nginx_config_active() = true, indicated by
    the X-Cache-Status header), where Nginx reads Redis keys directly without PHP
    and cannot compute hashes. The condition is now correctly gated on both
    is_nginx() AND nginx_config_active().
  • UX FIX: The plugin no longer lets users save a salt and then tells them it
    won’t work. When Nginx direct-Redis IS active (the true conflict case):

    • Basic settings tab: the Generate/Save form is replaced entirely by a yellow
      conflict notice explaining the incompatibility, with a one-click “Clear Salt”
      button if a broken salt is already set. The salt field is never shown.
    • Pro settings tab: same conflict notice appears above the salt field when
      nginx_config_active() and a salt is set.
    • Dashboard security matrix: Layer I shows an “Nginx Conflict” warning badge
      instead of “Active — SHA-256” so the problem is visible from the dashboard.
      When Nginx direct-Redis is NOT active (the normal case for this server):
    • No warning of any kind — salt generates and saves cleanly.

1.2.5

  • UX FIX: Security Hardening Matrix — all three layer badges are now context-
    aware instead of showing a generic “Active / Inactive”:

    • Layer I (Salt): “Active — SHA-256” when set, “Not configured” when not.
      Badge is orange-warn when unset instead of grey-inactive.
    • Layer II (ACL): “Socket-secured” when connected via Unix socket (OS file
      permissions are the ACL — no password needed); “Recommended” in orange-warn
      when on TCP without a password; “Active” when password is set.
    • Layer III (Socket): “Optimal” when Unix socket is active; “Using TCP” in
      blue-info (not alarming red-inactive) when on TCP.
    • Card meta text updated: “Configure in the Settings tab” instead of the
      old “Set wp-config.php constants to activate”.
  • UX FIX: Layer I (Cryptographic Key Salting) is no longer a PRO-only feature.
    An inline editable form now appears in the Security Hardening card on the
    basic Settings tab: type a salt or click Generate (uses crypto.getRandomValues)
    then Save. The save uses a dedicated lumencache_save_salt handler that only
    touches cache_salt — all other settings are preserved.
  • FIX: Security matrix $salt_on and $pass_on checks now use Settings::get() so
    values saved via the UI (DB option) are correctly reflected — previously both
    checked wp-config.php constants only, so UI-saved values always showed as
    inactive.
  • FIX: lumen-cache-proxy.php now reads ALL settings (salt, password, socket,
    host, port, prefix, db, timeout, cache_query_strings) from lumen-cache-
    config.php as a fallback when the corresponding wp-config.php constant is
    absent. Previously it fell back to built-in defaults, so Apache users with
    salt or password configured via the plugin UI had key mismatches between
    what PHP wrote and what the proxy looked up.

1.2.4

  • FIX: lumen-cache-proxy.php (Apache/LiteSpeed proxy) was missing the tracking-
    param stripping introduced in v1.2.2. Apache users whose traffic comes from
    Google Shopping (?srsltid=…) or Google/Meta Ads (?gclid=, ?fbclid=…) would
    always MISS the proxy cache because the key was built from the raw URL while
    the PHP plugin wrote under the stripped key. Also added a query-string bypass
    check to the proxy (mirrors advanced-cache.php behaviour).
  • FIX: The drop-in config snapshot (lumen-cache-config.php) was missing the
    cache_query_strings setting. The advanced-cache.php drop-in checks only the
    LUMENCACHE_CACHE_QUERY_STRINGS constant, so Pro users who enabled query-string
    caching via the admin UI (DB option) saw no effect. class-drop-in.php
    write_config() now writes cache_query_strings and advanced-cache.php reads
    it as a fallback when the constant is not defined.
  • FIX: WP-CLI wp lumen-cache status showed Host/Port/TTL sourced from raw
    constants only — ignoring DB settings saved via the admin UI. Changed to
    use Settings::effective_connection() and Settings::get() so the output
    matches the actual running configuration.
  • FIX: Dashboard zero-cache panel only showed a warning when the drop-in was NOT
    deployed. When the drop-in was deployed but the cache was empty (e.g. after
    a flush), the panel was silent. A green informational notice is now shown
    explaining that the cache populates on anonymous visits.

1.2.3

  • CRITICAL FIX: key_count() and delete_pattern() used the wrong phpredis SCAN
    API. phpredis scan() updates the cursor by reference and returns just the
    keys array — the code was treating the return as [$cursor, $keys] (Predis
    format). So (int)$result[0] cast the first cached-page key string to 0,
    the loop exited after one batch, and the cached-pages counter always showed
    0 even when hundreds of pages were cached. The flush operation had the same
    bug and deleted only one key per call, leaving 700MB+ of unreachable entries
    in Redis. Fixed: phpredis branch now uses $cursor by reference (initialized
    to null), reads keys directly from the return value, and loops while($cursor).
    Predis branch unchanged.

1.2.2

  • CRITICAL FIX: Tracking-param bypass — every URL from Google Shopping arrives
    with ?srsltid=… appended; every Google Ads URL with ?gclid=…; every Meta Ads
    URL with ?fbclid=…. The query-string bypass check was treating these as
    content-affecting parameters and refusing to cache any of those requests.
    On a perfume shop where Google Shopping is a primary traffic source, this
    caused 0 cached pages. Root cause confirmed via LUMENCACHE_DEBUG trace.
    Fix: strip 14 known tracking params (srsltid, gclid, gclsrc, gbraid, wbraid,
    fbclid, msclkid, ttclid, twclid, li_fat_id, _ga, _gl, mc_eid, yclid) before
    the bypass check AND before building the cache key. Non-tracking query params
    (in_stock, page, s, etc.) are preserved as before. The same stripping is
    applied in both class-cache-engine.php and advanced-cache.php (drop-in) so
    HIT and MISS paths use identical keys. Pages with only tracking tokens (most
    Google/Meta ad traffic) now cache correctly on the first organic visit.

1.2.1

  • FIX: connect_phpredis() now checks return value of Redis::connect() — a false
    return (connection refused) no longer silently reports as connected.
  • FIX: nginx_map_block() removed wp_woocommerce_session_ bypass — this was
    inconsistent with the v1.1.0 PHP-side fix and would have caused 0% Nginx
    HIT rates on WooCommerce sites (session cookie set for all visitors).
  • FIX: nginx_server_block() now generates unix:/path redis_pass when a Unix
    socket is configured, instead of always generating TCP host:port.
  • FIX: Layer III security_row tagline had double esc_html() (sprintf pre-escaped
    address, then security_row() escaped the whole string again).
  • FIX: Dashboard widget warning now correctly fires when drop-in is deployed but
    no pages are cached, with accurate message. Old message said “pages ARE
    cached” when count was 0 — a logical contradiction.
  • FIX: maybe_write_cache() no longer redundantly calls should_bypass() at shutdown
    when start_capture() already confirmed bypass=false at template_redirect.
    Eliminates edge-case false positives from WP functions at shutdown.
  • NEW: LUMENCACHE_DEBUG mode — define(‘LUMENCACHE_DEBUG’, true) in wp-config.php
    writes a full per-step trace of every cache decision to lc-debug.log in
    wp-content/. Remove constant after diagnosing; log grows indefinitely.
  • MINOR: version comment in admin.js and admin.css updated from v1.1.0 to v1.2.1.

1.2.0

  • FIX: Write-path rebuilt for PHP-FPM + Nginx FastCGI environments. LumenCache
    now calls ob_start() at template_redirect priority 0 to own its output
    buffer. At shutdown priority 0, ob_get_contents() reads our inner buffer
    and ob_end_flush() passes the HTML up to WordPress’s outer buffer so
    pages are cached AND the browser receives them correctly.
  • FIX: Dashboard “Nginx configuration not active” warning replaced with a
    smarter drop-in deployment check — no more false alarms on PHP-FPM hosts.
  • IMPROVEMENT: Settings tab rebuilt for Basic / Pro licensing model.
    Basic shows auto-detected Redis connection as read-only cards.
    Pro (LUMENCACHE_PRO_LICENSE constant) unlocks full editable form.
  • IMPROVEMENT: “Nginx / Apache Proxy Bridge” renamed to “Nginx Direct RAM Bridge”
    throughout Dashboard and Server Setup.
  • IMPROVEMENT: Security Matrix updated — Layer I: Cryptographic Key Salting,
    Layer II: ACL Isolation, Layer III: Unix Socket Lockdown.
  • IMPROVEMENT: Settings auto-detects Unix socket (probes /var/run/redis/redis.sock
    and fallbacks); effective_connection() used for display and security matrix.
  • IMPROVEMENT: Server Setup tab — PHP Proxy Mode primary card removed. Drop-in
    status shown as compact status rows. Nginx Direct RAM Bridge is the main
    blueprint (not hidden in ).
  • VERSION: Bumped to 1.2.0.

1.1.1

  • NEW: advanced-cache.php WordPress drop-in — serves Redis-cached pages before
    WordPress, plugins, or the database load. Works on ALL web servers with
    no Nginx module required.
  • NEW: class-drop-in.php — manages drop-in deployment, config file, and
    WP_CACHE detection / automatic wp-config.php modification.
  • FIX: Nginx “unknown directive redis_pass” — requires ngx_http_redis module
    which most Plesk / managed Nginx builds do not include. PHP Proxy Mode
    (advanced-cache.php) is now the primary setup; zero server …

short_description: RAM-first full-page caching that serves pages before WordPress loads, with automatic WooCommerce and LMS integration.
description:
LumenCache implements a RAM-first full-page cache with a WordPress
advanced-cache.php drop-in. On a cache HIT, the drop-in serves complete HTML
before the normal WordPress bootstrap and database queries. This early-response
path reduces application-layer work and keeps repeat page requests fast across
Nginx, Apache, and LiteSpeed.

The cache is designed to fail open when its storage layer is unavailable, so a
cache connection problem does not take the WordPress site offline.

Research Foundation

Academic Reference:
“Dynamic Resource Mapping in Zero-Reload Server Architectures: Eliminating
Application-Layer Latency and Extension Dependency in High-Concurrency CMS
personalised requests continue through the full WordPress stack.

This architecture is intended to reduce repeated bootstrap work, database
queries, and extension overhead while preserving WordPress compatibility. It
also provides a practical bridge between academic performance research and
everyday publishing workloads, including content-heavy sites, WooCommerce
catalogues, and membership-driven pages.

Research author: Dean Nasrul Eam — Light & Composition University.

Eight-Subsystem Architecture

  1. RAM-First Full-Page Cache Engine — PHP stores complete HTML at
    shutdown and resolves repeat requests from the in-memory cache layer.
  2. Nginx / Apache Proxy Bridge — Static or dynamic server config bypasses
    PHP entirely for cache hits.
  3. Selective Bypass Cookie Router — sys_active_state cookie routes
    logged-in users and cart-active visitors to live PHP.
  4. Application Driver Profile Engine — Auto-detects WooCommerce,
    LearnDash, LifterLMS, MemberPress, BuddyBoss and registers tailored bypass
    rules and invalidation hooks.
  5. Surgical Cache Invalidation — Post save / nav menu / widget / theme
    switch events trigger precise per-URL or full purges.
  6. REST API State Endpoint — /wp-json/lumencache/v1/user-state serves
    personalised fragments for skeleton-hydration clients.
  7. Skeleton Hydration DOM Worker — skeleton-hydration.js replaces cached
    placeholders with live content on load.
  8. WP-CLI Management Interface — flush, flush-url, status commands.

Configuration (optional)

All settings are configurable from LumenCache → Settings in the WordPress
admin. Optionally override any setting via wp-config.php — constants always win:

define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_HOST',          '127.0.0.1' );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_PORT',          6379 );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_SOCKET',        '' );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_PASSWORD',      '' );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_DATABASE',      0 );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_TIMEOUT',       1.0 );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_REDIS_PREFIX',        'cache:' );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_CACHE_TTL',           86400 );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_CACHE_SALT',          '' );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_CACHE_QUERY_STRINGS', false );
define( 'LUMENCACHE_PROXY_PASSWORD',      '' );

WP-CLI

wp lumencache flush
wp lumencache flush-url https://example.com/page/
wp lumencache status<h3>Privacy</h3>

LumenCache stores rendered page HTML and cache metadata in the in-memory cache
service configured by the site administrator. It does not send cache contents,
visitor data, or analytics data to a third-party LumenCache service. The
optional user-state endpoint returns only the requested dynamic values to the
requesting browser; sites should review those values and their own privacy
policy before enabling personalized hydration.

Current Active Pipeline Status — LumenCache + LumenCache Pro (August 8, 2026)

Audited release: LumenCache 1.6.3 / LumenCache Pro 1.0.5. Every listed
pipeline was read from its UI/request entry point through configuration,
runtime, failures, persistence, invalidation, and visible output.

  • Pre-WordPress readers (drop-in and Apache proxy): fixed Redis timeout,
    Predis availability, boolean configuration parsing, empty-value reader
    parity, and safety bypasses for dynamic/personal routes. Confirmed tracking
    key stripping and Redis key construction agree with the write path.
  • Capture and Redis write: fixed non-HTML response rejection; full-page
    cache stores only HTML that early readers can safely replay.
  • Local invalidation and purge controls: fixed relative URL, host/scheme,
    trailing-slash, and tracking-query normalization so admin/CLI/post purges
    target the same key cache writes create.
  • Server integration and lifecycle: fixed foreign drop-in overwrite; LumenCache
    owns/removes only its own file. Generated Apache/Nginx configuration and
    existing salt safety behavior were read directly.
  • Application drivers and state routing: fixed early-reader parity for
    WooCommerce, LMS, membership, Buddy/BuddyPress, and LCU routes/cookies; no
    longer clears active-session state on completion events that do not end access.
  • Administration, REST, CLI, updates: verified capability/nonce boundaries;
    fixed REST personalized-state access, update-domain identity/PHP metadata,
    LumenCache screen asset scoping, and visible drop-in conflict feedback.
  • Pro entitlement, telemetry, Cloudflare, updates and UI: fixed
    constant-license update eligibility and Cloudflare token page-source exposure.
    Local-first then best-effort edge invalidation and license status/drop-in
    synchronization were verified.
  • Intentional constraints retained: domain-only license authorization and
    the optional direct-Redis Nginx tracking-parameter limitation remain
    unchanged by design. Standard Nginx cannot use salted SHA-256 keys without
    the documented OpenResty/Lua route.
  • Validation: focused regression contracts pass (13 tests / 60 assertions);
    all LumenCache and LumenCache Pro PHP files lint clean. A real
    WordPress+Redis+Cloudflare server remains required to prove live edge/API
    behavior after installation.

upgrade_notice.1.1.0: Critical fix: WooCommerce sites will see dramatically improved cache hit rates after upgrading (session cookie over-bypass resolved). Also adds admin settings panel — no wp-config.php editing required for basic setup.
